rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 5 (score 521.7) is the best design so far: seven sensors at x = -0.075 to +0.075 m (0.025 m spacing), y = 0.07 m, sensor size 0.016 m, kp 5.0, kd 0.6, ki 0, base_speed 1.1. It finishes the oval 20/20 at 1.99 s, reaches s-bend progress 0.78 (5/20 finishes) and slalom progress 0.40. Denser sensing was the one change that clearly helped. Iteration 6 widened the array to x = +/-0.08 m and moved it forward to y = 0.08 m. That dropped s-bend progress to 0.47 and slalom to 0.32, and the score fell to 424. So the wider, more forward array is worse, and I am reverting to the iteration 5 geometry. All remaining failures are off_track with max_error 0.059 to 0.064 m, just past the fixed 0.06 m limit, with low steering oscillation (0.25 to 0.43). The robot lags on bends rather than jittering. Iterations 3 and 4 showed that raising kp or kd, or adding ki, hurt the oval, so I keep the gains.

Change (one variable, controller only): base_speed 1.1 -> 1.0. On the tightest bends the robot is still too fast for its correction. Iteration 4 lowered speed together with a gain change, so its effect was never isolated. Here the geometry and gains match iteration 5, so any change in s-bend and slalom progress can be read as a speed effect. Oval time should rise from about 1.99 s to about 2.2 s, which still leaves room under the 3 s limit.

Expected result: s-bend progress and finishes rise (target 0.85 or more, and at least 5 finishes out of 20). Slalom progress rises a little. Oval stays at 20/20. Score should rise modestly, or hold if the time cost dominates.

Hypotheses: H1, a slightly lower speed lets the existing proportional and derivative action keep the robot on the line through tight bends. H2, the oval finish rate holds, since the loop is unchanged apart from speed. H3, the time cost stays small, so the completion gain outweighs it.

Next measurements: completion and progress per track (do s-bend and slalom finish more often), completion_time (the cost of the slower speed), max_error and line_loss_events (where the line is still lost), and steering_oscillation (whether the loop is stable at this speed).
